Definition: from G444 and G700; man-courting, i.e. fawning:--men-pleaser.
BiblicalUsage: Paul warns servants to serve with singleness of heart, not with eyeservice as menpleasers, but as the servants of Christ. The word names the man who works only to be seen, courting the favour of men rather than God.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for menpleasers carries no teaching of its own; its warning is Paul's, that work done only for watching eyes is not service to Christ.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
